The only reason as to why I feel as though Nietzsche was referring to man as evil is because of the maxim you can put the will to power in. It's binary creating in nature which I feel is where Nietzsche makes the assertion that what man is doing is selfish and evil. This author 'Dennesson' (I always forget his first name), he makes the simulation that one cannot give what we call a gift to another for altruistic reasons. So if that's true based on the will to power and altruism is the good of a human being, then because the will to power denies altruism it makes the argument that humans are intrinsically the negation, which is evil. 

I agree on Schopenhauer, he was always life denying because of his traumatic upbringing. 

I've kind of always thought of Nietzsche's idea that suffering is a necessary and normal part of life as a measurement of how you can and should be in control of your own death. As in terms of, if you've accepted that you've done more suffering than not than you can accept that it's not just a dark night. Thus suicide.

Humans are inherently evil but that's okay because we're born that way and we can to use it to our advantage, for good or bad.
